text:
Maria Chen: heads-up — Fennel customer reported odd output after we merged their LoRA into `fennel-base-v2`. Short examples show token shifts in invoice amounts, sometimes duplicated numbers. Filing quick triage here. Anyone available to run a focused eval pack?

Jon Park: I'm free for the next hour. Can you drop the artifact links (model + lora) and the exact prompt set that reproduces? I'll spin up a quick-int4 shadow run. :eyes:

Maria Chen: artifact: s3://redwood-custs/fennel/lora/2026-03-20/fennel-amt-lora.tar.gz, base: fennel-base-v2-int4, promptset: gist.github.com/maria/fennel-invoice-12cases (public for our infra only). Repro steps: the model returns amounts like `1,200` -> `12,00` or duplicates `1200 1200`. Happens more on long-context invoices (>512 tokens).

Siva Raman: sounds like a tokenizer offset or kv-cache alignment issue after merging. Did we do remapping for LoRA that touches embedding table indices? If the LoRA was trained on a different BPE vocab ordering it can cause token boundary changes.

Tara Li: also flagging quantization interactions — we saw similar duplicated numeric tokens with int4 kernels when row-wise quantization + per-channel scale is borderline. Could be amplification of a tiny logit shift. I can add a control run w/ fp16 to see if it persists.

eval-bot: quick-eval (run id: qe-3287)
- dataset: fennel-invoice-12cases
- model: fennel-base-v2-int4 + lora-20260320
- metrics: exact-amount-match: 66%, numeric-duplication-rate: 14%, token-shift-rate: 9%

Jon Park: thanks. I'll run the following locally and share outputs:
```bash
# quick shadow run
redwood run --model fennel-base-v2-int4 --lora s3://.../fennel-amt-lora.tar.gz \
  --prompts ./fennel-invoice-12cases.json --quant-mode int4 --emit-logs
```
Expecting to reproduce. If so, next step is fp16 baseline + int4 with kvcache-offset debug prints.

Siva Raman: ran the shadow with `--debug-kv-offset` — early results attached:
```
[dbg] prompt_id=03 offset_delta=0x0
[dbg] prompt_id=07 offset_delta=0x4  <-- suspicious
[dbg] token_stream: 1200, 1200
```
Looks like an offset_delta on the chunk boundary for long ctx which correlates with duplication. Investigating whether LoRA merge changed kv indices.

Tara Li: fp16 run (no quant) gives exact-amount-match: 95%, duplication-rate: 0%. So quantization interaction strongly implicated.

Maria Chen: good catch. Ops: can we try regenerating the merged checkpoint but remapping embeddings through our `lora-remap` utility (handles vocab reorder and kv index stablization)? If that fixes, we can produce a recommended rebuild for the customer and a mitigation doc.

Jon Park: I'll trigger remap+remerge and run the quick-eval suite. Assigning: Jon -> remap+eval, Siva -> deeper kvtrace for other prompts, Tara -> perf/quant config suggestions and recommended flags. I'll post results here in ~45m. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: perfect — if remap fixes, we'll create a short release note and a Redirection policy to prefer remapped artifacts for Dedicated deployments. :+1:
